podcast.title: 1990s Nationalism
podcast.body: The 1990s saw a significant rise in Canadian nationalism for domestic music, creating a fertile environment for bands like Big Wreck, The Tragically Hip, The Watchmen, Headstones, The Tea Party, Moist, Our Lady Peace, and I Mother Earth. This period was characterized by a "huge tsunami of popular, powerful Canadian music." "all through the 90s, we seem to have developed a nationalism for domestic music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ian Thornley - In His Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: 1990s Renaissance/Revolution
podcast.body: The early 1990s marked a "Canadian rock Renaissance" or "revolution," where bands like The Headstones, The Tragically Hip, Our Lady Peace, I Mother Earth, Moist, and Sloan simultaneously emerged. This movement helped correct the widespread perception that Canadian music was substandard, fostering fierce nationalistic pride and demand for Canadian artists, with The Tragically Hip serving as a unifying force. "So this is 92 93. So we're at the beginning of this this Canadian rock Renaissance or this can rock revolution."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
